IN-DOR.registration: Register the employer for withholding through INBiz with its EIN. Use INTIME to manage the account.
returns: WH-1

Report county amounts by county code on the state withholding return. For annual filers the DOR handbook lists January 30 and the DOR filing calendar lists January 31. Confirm the assigned deadline in INTIME or with DOR. Monthly filers are due 30 days after month end and early monthly filers 20 days after month end. Use the frequency assigned by DOR.
WH-3
Reconcile annually by January 31, with the wage statements. Continue required returns for zero periods while registered.
IN-DOR.filing: File electronically through INTIME. Registered bulk filers can use SFTP under DOR specifications.
IN-DOR.payment: Pay electronically through INTIME. An electronic filing exemption must be resolved with DOR before relying on paper.

OH-SDIT.registration: Register when an employee lives in a taxing school district. Use the existing Ohio employer withholding account if already registered.
returns: SD 101

Report school district withholding by district. Quarterly remittances are due at the end of the next month. Monthly remittances are due on the 15th of the next month. Use the school district frequency assigned to the account.
SD 141
Reconcile each district by January 31 of the next year, or within 15 days after discontinuing business.
OH-SDIT.filing: File electronically through OH|TAX eServices. Preserve four-digit school district numbers including leading zeros.
OH-SDIT.payment: Remit electronically through the state withholding service. The state partial-weekly rule is for state withholding.

OH-RITA.registration: Register the business and its municipality through MyAccount, online registration, or paper Form 48.
returns: Quarterly due at the end of the next month. Monthly due on the 15th of the next month. If the municipality requires semimonthly remittance, due three banking days after the 15th and month end. Consult the municipality-specific frequency and threshold rules.
Annual reconciliation and wage statement transmittal due by the last day of February.
Use to adjust an earlier employer statement.
OH-RITA.filing: Use MyAccount for electronic filing and W-2 upload. Paper form downloads and form-specific mailing addresses are published separately.
OH-RITA.payment: Remit through MyAccount or mail a check with the appropriate payment remittance when permitted.

OH-CCA.collector: City of Cleveland, Central Collection Agency
OH-CCA.registration: Complete CCA online business registration before signing in to eFile.
returns: Employer’s Return of Income Tax Withheld

Quarterly due at the end of the following month. Monthly due on the 15th of the following month. Semimonthly due three banking days after the 15th and month end for applicable municipalities and accounts.
Submit written annual reconciliation and W-2 information by the last day of February. CCA requires electronic media for 10 or more W-2s.
OH-CCA.filing: Use CCA eFile for monthly or quarterly returns. Report employment and residence cities separately. Use CCA’s published employer form for paper filing.
OH-CCA.payment: Use the payment step in eFile, or send a check payable to CCA with the paper return.

OH-OAKWOOD-MONTGOMERY.collector: City of Oakwood Income Tax Department (Montgomery County)
OH-OAKWOOD-MONTGOMERY.registration: Contact the department at 937-298-0531 to obtain the employer withholding account number used with the FEIN on OW-1.
returns: OW-1

Monthly if prior calendar year withholding exceeded $2,399 or any month in the preceding quarter exceeded $200. Monthly returns are due 15 days after month end. Quarterly due dates for 2026 wages are April 30, July 31, November 2 and February 1, 2027.
OW-3
Annual reconciliation with W-2s. The city's standing instructions specify February 28. Confirm the 2026 year-end form and actual filing date with the department.
OH-OAKWOOD-MONTGOMERY.filing: Mail the 2026 OW-1 to City of Oakwood, Income Tax Department, PO Box 269, Eaton Rapids, MI 48827.
OH-OAKWOOD-MONTGOMERY.payment: Enclose remittance with OW-1 using the department's lockbox address.

OH-DELTA.collector: Village of Delta Income Tax Department
OH-DELTA.registration: Submit the village business income tax questionnaire. Confirm the employer account and filing schedule with the income tax administrator at 419-822-3190 ext. 102.
returns: Report withholding for the assigned period. The village publishes a quarterly W-1. Confirm the applicable deadline and frequency with the village.
Annual withholding reconciliation. Contact the village about 2026 year-end submissions due after the January 1, 2027 RITA transition.
OH-DELTA.filing: For village-administered filings, mail signed forms to 401 Main Street, Delta, OH 43515.
OH-DELTA.payment: Remit withheld tax to the village with W-1. Confirm the recipient before paying after the transition.

PA-KEYSTONE-LST.registration: Confirm the worksite LST collector in Pennsylvania DCED’s address search. Create an account at https://business.keystonecollects.com and register the employer using its FEIN and worksite information.
returns: Quarterly Return for Employer – Local Services Tax
File and remit within 30 days after quarter end. Use the zero-filing option if all employees are exempt.
PA-KEYSTONE-LST.filing: Select Local Services Tax in the Business Portal. Keystone directs 2026 LST employers to use its electronic filing process.
PA-KEYSTONE-LST.payment: Submit the LST payment electronically through the Business Portal.

PA-BERKHEIMER-LST.registration: Confirm the worksite LST collector in Pennsylvania DCED’s address search. Use Berkheimer Employer Registration to obtain the HAB employer account number, or look up an existing account. Register for e-file to submit online.
returns: LST-1
File and remit within 30 days after quarter end. Include the required employee list with the return.
PA-BERKHEIMER-LST.filing: File LST-1 through Berkheimer employer e-file by online entry or supported file upload, or send the paper form to HAB-LST, PO Box 25156, Lehigh Valley, PA 18002.
PA-BERKHEIMER-LST.payment: Pay online when filing online, or include the remittance with a mailed LST-1.

MI-DETROIT.collector: Michigan Department of Treasury, City Tax Administration
MI-DETROIT.registration: Register for Michigan withholding and use the employer FEIN for Detroit. A business already registered for Michigan withholding uses that registration.
returns: File every month, including zero-liability months. Return and payment are due on the 15th of the following month.

File the annual reconciliation with employee W-2 information by the last day of February. The next-business-day rule moves the 2026 deadline to March 1, 2027. On discontinuance, file by the final withholding payment deadline.
MI-DETROIT.filing: File Detroit returns with Michigan Treasury. The city withholding e-file program accepts returns through supported tax software. Follow the 5321 instructions for W-2 submission.
MI-DETROIT.payment: Remit monthly withholding electronically using Treasury EFT debit or credit. For debit enrollment or an account update, use Form 5473.

MI-GRAND-RAPIDS.collector: City of Grand Rapids Income Tax Department
MI-GRAND-RAPIDS.registration: Submit the city’s SS-4 Withholding Registration. Obtain your employer’s customized withholding booklet from the city or its online service.
returns: Withholding return / deposit
File quarterly by the last day of the following month. If withholding exceeds $100 in the first or second month of a quarter, deposit that month’s withholding by the end of the next month.
GR-W-3
Reconcile annually by February 28 and attach W-2 detail and any balance due.
MI-GRAND-RAPIDS.filing: Use the File or Pay Employer Withholding link on the city website or mail the city forms to Grand Rapids City Income Tax, PO Box 347, Grand Rapids, MI 49501.
MI-GRAND-RAPIDS.payment: Pay through the city’s employer withholding service or include payment with the mailed return.

MI-LANSING.collector: City of Lansing Income Tax Department
MI-LANSING.registration: Complete Lansing’s L-SS-4 employer withholding registration with your FEIN and worksite details.
returns: File quarterly by the end of the following month. Deposit earlier when withholding exceeds $100 in the first or second month of the quarter, by the end of the next month.
LW-3
Submit the annual reconciliation with employee W-2s by February 28.
MI-LANSING.filing: Use Lansing’s employer withholding service or submit the L-941 voucher with the remittance to the City of Lansing Treasurer, PO Box 19219, Lansing, MI 48901.
MI-LANSING.payment: Pay online by ACH debit or mail a check or money order with the L-941 voucher.

MI-EAST-LANSING.collector: City of East Lansing Income Tax Department
MI-EAST-LANSING.registration: Submit EL-SS-4, then set up the employer account in East Lansing’s Employer Withholding Tool.
returns: For the first and second months of each quarter, deposit the month’s withholding if it exceeds $100. Use the monthly due dates in the 2026 employer packet.
Report all quarterly withholding and remit the undeposited balance. For 2026 the quarterly due dates are April 30, July 31, November 2 and February 1, 2027.
EL-W-3
File the annual reconciliation and W-2s by the last day of February following the tax year. Identify East Lansing in W-2 box 20.
MI-EAST-LANSING.filing: File through East Lansing’s Employer Withholding Tool or use the forms and instructions in its 2026 packet.
MI-EAST-LANSING.payment: Use the city’s online employer withholding payment service or remit with the appropriate EL-501 or EL-941 voucher.

MI-ALBION.collector: City of Albion Income Tax Department
MI-ALBION.registration: Submit the City of Albion Employer Registration Packet and complete the EFT enrollment for the payment method selected.
returns: AL-941 M / Q
Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
AL-W3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-ALBION.filing: Use the assigned monthly or quarterly AL-941. Employers remitting by EFT can omit the periodic paper return. The annual AL-W3 is filed on paper.
MI-ALBION.payment: Use the enrolled ACH method. For ACH credit, send the test transaction required by the city. Pay any balance on the annual paper reconciliation by check or money order.

MI-BATTLE-CREEK.collector: City of Battle Creek Income Tax Department
MI-BATTLE-CREEK.registration: Contact Battle Creek Income Tax with the employer FEIN and worksite details to establish the account and obtain the appropriate BC-941 series.
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
BC W-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-BATTLE-CREEK.filing: Send the signed monthly or quarterly BC-941 to Battle Creek Income Tax, PO Box 1657, Battle Creek, MI 49016-1657. Include W-2s with the annual reconciliation.
MI-BATTLE-CREEK.payment: Include a check or money order payable to the City of Battle Creek.

MI-BENTON-HARBOR.collector: City of Benton Harbor Income Tax Department
MI-BENTON-HARBOR.registration: Complete the COBH Employer Registration Form on the city’s income tax forms page.
returns: Monthly deposit / quarterly return

Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
CF-W3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-BENTON-HARBOR.filing: Use the vouchers in Benton Harbor’s 2026 withholding booklet and its separate 2026 CF-W3.
MI-BENTON-HARBOR.payment: Make remittance payable to the City of Benton Harbor and send it to the address on the applicable voucher.

MI-BIG-RAPIDS.collector: City of Big Rapids Income Tax Department
MI-BIG-RAPIDS.registration: Return the city’s Employer Registration form to the Big Rapids Income Tax Office with employer identification and the date taxable wages were first paid.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
BRW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-BIG-RAPIDS.filing: Send BR-941 with the employer ID to the city Income Tax Office at 226 North Michigan Avenue, Big Rapids, MI 49307. File a quarterly return even for a zero quarter.
MI-BIG-RAPIDS.payment: Make remittance payable to the City of Big Rapids.

MI-FLINT.collector: City of Flint Income Tax Department
MI-FLINT.registration: Register with F-SS-4 before activating Flint’s withholding tool with the assigned account number.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
FW3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-FLINT.filing: Use Flint’s withholding service or the vouchers in the city’s 2026 employer packet.
MI-FLINT.payment: Pay through Flint’s employer withholding site or mail the payment and voucher as directed in the packet.

MI-GRAYLING.collector: City of Grayling Income Tax Department
MI-GRAYLING.registration: Submit Grayling’s GR-SS-4 employer registration form.
returns: The city instructs quarterly filing by the end of the next month, including zero periods, and offers monthly reporting on request. Confirm deposit frequency with the city if withholding exceeds the statutory $100 threshold.
GRW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-GRAYLING.filing: File paper GR-941 returns with the City of Grayling Income Tax Division, PO Box 549, Grayling, MI 49738. Use that address for current and past periods administered by the city.
MI-GRAYLING.payment: Include a check payable to the City of Grayling.

MI-HAMTRAMCK.collector: City of Hamtramck Income Tax Department
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
HW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-HAMTRAMCK.filing: Use the appropriate 2026 Hamtramck voucher packet and send the signed periodic voucher to its withholding lockbox, PO Box 209, Eaton Rapids, MI 48827.
MI-HAMTRAMCK.payment: Make the remittance payable to the Treasurer, City of Hamtramck.

MI-HIGHLAND-PARK.collector: City of Highland Park Income Tax Department
MI-HIGHLAND-PARK.registration: Submit Highland Park’s HP-SS-4 business and withholding registration.
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
HPW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-HIGHLAND-PARK.filing: Use Highland Park’s 2026 vouchers. The periodic withholding payment lockbox is PO Box 239, Eaton Rapids, MI 48827.
MI-HIGHLAND-PARK.payment: Make the remittance payable to the Treasurer, City of Highland Park.

MI-HUDSON.collector: City of Hudson Income Tax Department
MI-HUDSON.registration: Contact Hudson’s Income Tax Office at 517-448-8983 for employer account setup and the HU-941.
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
HUW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-HUDSON.filing: Submit HU-941 for the assigned monthly or quarterly period and HUW-3 with employee W-2s at year end.
MI-HUDSON.payment: Send payment with HU-941 using the instructions provided by the city Income Tax Office.

MI-IONIA.collector: City of Ionia Income Tax Department
MI-IONIA.registration: Submit Ionia’s Business Withholding Registration Form.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
IW-3

Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year. The 2026 booklet introduction prints a date before year end. Confirm the year-specific IW-3 deadline with Ionia.
MI-IONIA.filing: Use I-501 for interim deposits and I-941 for quarterly reporting. Use MI-ION in W-2 box 20. The city accepts W-2 data on CD-ROM or USB under its specifications.
MI-IONIA.payment: Make the voucher remittance payable to the City of Ionia.

MI-JACKSON.collector: City of Jackson Income Tax Department
MI-JACKSON.registration: Register with the Jackson Income Tax Office using its Employer Withholding Registration form and FEIN. Payroll providers should request a portal invitation.
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-JACKSON.filing: Use Jackson’s employer site for annual W-3 e-filing and monthly or quarterly remittances. J-941 vouchers are also published for 2026.
MI-JACKSON.payment: Pay online through the employer account or send a check with J-941 to the Treasurer, City of Jackson.

MI-LAPEER.collector: City of Lapeer Income Tax Department
MI-LAPEER.registration: Register the employer with Lapeer’s L-SS-4.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month. Lapeer’s guide lists July 30 alongside a month-end rule. Confirm the Q2 date before relying on July 31.
LW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-LAPEER.filing: Use the city withholding service for L-941 and LW-3. File L-941 for every active quarter, including quarters with no withholding.
MI-LAPEER.payment: Use the withholding payment option on Lapeer’s tax site or remit with the city voucher.

MI-MUSKEGON.collector: City of Muskegon Income Tax Department
MI-MUSKEGON.registration: Register with the Muskegon Income Tax Department using M-SS-4 and activate the employer withholding account.
returns: Withholding voucher

Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
MW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-MUSKEGON.filing: Complete MW-3 through Muskegon’s eWithholding service. If mailing a periodic payment, print the voucher from that service.
MI-MUSKEGON.payment: Pay through eWithholding or mail payment with the printed voucher. The city directs employers paying online to omit the duplicate mailed voucher.

MI-MUSKEGON-HEIGHTS.collector: City of Muskegon Heights Income Tax Department
MI-MUSKEGON-HEIGHTS.registration: Register through the employer registration link on the City of Muskegon Heights tax site using the business FEIN.
returns: Employer withholding payment

Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
Employer’s annual reconciliation

Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year. The city page shows an inconsistent prior-year example. Confirm the 2026 filing date in the employer account.
MI-MUSKEGON-HEIGHTS.filing: Manage withholding and complete the annual reconciliation on the Muskegon Heights withholding website.
MI-MUSKEGON-HEIGHTS.payment: The city directs employers to make all withholding payments online.

MI-PONTIAC.collector: City of Pontiac Income Tax Department
MI-PONTIAC.registration: Register the employer FEIN on Pontiac P-SS-4. The city advises that it does not issue a registration confirmation.
returns: Use the city’s monthly or quarterly voucher for the assigned period. Remit by the end of the following month.
PW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-PONTIAC.filing: Mail P-941 and remittance to City of Pontiac Income Tax Division, PO Box 530, Eaton Rapids, MI 48827-0530.
MI-PONTIAC.payment: Make the check payable to Treasurer, City of Pontiac and include the FEIN.

MI-PORT-HURON.collector: City of Port Huron Income Tax Department
MI-PORT-HURON.registration: Register with the City of Port Huron using PH-2.
returns: PH-941 and payment are due by the end of the month after each quarter. The city permits a monthly election and asks for 30 days’ notice to switch back. Confirm the deposit schedule with the office if withholding exceeds $100.
PH-W3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-PORT-HURON.filing: Submit PH-941 to the city. Include W-2 information with PH-W3. Employers with 100 or more employees must use electronic media for W-2s.
MI-PORT-HURON.payment: Send a check payable to Treasurer, City of Port Huron with the periodic voucher.

MI-PORTLAND.collector: City of Portland Income Tax Department
MI-PORTLAND.registration: Register the FEIN with Portland using P-SS-4.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
PW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-PORTLAND.filing: Submit P-941 with the applicable withholding payment. File PW-3 with copies of employee W-2s.
MI-PORTLAND.payment: Mail a check or money order payable to the City of Portland with the voucher.

MI-SAGINAW.collector: City of Saginaw Income Tax Department
MI-SAGINAW.registration: Register with Saginaw on S-SS-4 and obtain a PIN for the city withholding website.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
SW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-SAGINAW.filing: Complete S-501, S-941 and SW-3 in the city’s online preparation tool. A quarterly S-941 is required even for zero withholding.
MI-SAGINAW.payment: Follow the city’s deposit instructions. Mailed checks are payable to Saginaw City Treasurer.

MI-SPRINGFIELD.collector: City of Springfield Income Tax Department
MI-SPRINGFIELD.registration: Contact Springfield’s Income Tax Department to establish the withholding account. Include the FEIN and the business start date on the first SF-941.
returns: Springfield’s instructions call for monthly deposits when withholding is $100 or more in a month, due at the end of the next month. Otherwise deposit quarterly by the end of the next month. This includes exactly $100 under the city’s instructions.
SF W-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-SPRINGFIELD.filing: Send SF-941 to City of Springfield Income Tax Department, 601 Avenue A, Springfield, MI 49037-7774.
MI-SPRINGFIELD.payment: Include full remittance payable to the City of Springfield with the deposit voucher.

MI-WALKER.collector: City of Walker Income Tax Department
MI-WALKER.registration: Register in Walker’s Employer Withholding Tool.
returns: Quarterly returns and any remaining balance are due by the last day of the following month. When withholding exceeds $100 in either of the first two months of a quarter, deposit that month’s amount by the end of the following month.
WW-3
Reconcile the year’s withholding with employee wage statements by the last day of February following the tax year.
MI-WALKER.filing: Use the city tool for periodic vouchers and W-2s. Upload W-2s before submitting WW-3 electronically.
MI-WALKER.payment: Pay electronically in the tool or print the city voucher and remit to the Walker City Treasurer.

MO-KANSAS-CITY.collector: City of Kansas City, Missouri, Revenue Division
MO-KANSAS-CITY.registration: Complete the city registration application (RD-100) and establish the employer withholding account with the Revenue Division. Use Quick Tax for online filing.
returns: File every quarter, including a zero-withholding quarter, by the last day of the following month. If that date is a weekend or legal holiday, file the next business day. Report gross compensation and withholding and settle any remaining quarterly balance.
RD-130M / RD-130QM

Follow the state withholding remittance frequency assigned to the employer. Monthly remittances are due on the 15th of the following month except for the quarter’s final month, due at the following month end. Quarter-monthly periods end on the 7th, 15th, 22nd and last day of each month, with payment due three banking days later.
Reconcile annually by January 31 following the tax year. Submit W-2 detail for employees whose Kansas City earnings tax was withheld.
MO-KANSAS-CITY.filing: File RD-110 and RD-113 electronically in Kansas City Quick Tax. Payroll providers may use the city’s bulk filing program.
MO-KANSAS-CITY.payment: Pay electronically in Quick Tax. Apply interim remittances to the correct withholding period and report the remaining balance with RD-110.

MO-ST-LOUIS.collector: City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue
MO-ST-LOUIS.registration: Before beginning business in the city, submit Form E-9 to the Earnings Tax Department by mail, fax or email. The employer’s FEIN is its earnings tax account number.
returns: Report employee earnings tax withheld each quarter. The city lists April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 as the quarterly due dates.

Report employer payroll expense tax with the W-10 for the same quarter when applicable. The city lists exemptions, including qualifying nonprofits and businesses operating only at Lambert Airport. Confirm any exemption with the Collector.
Reconcile W-10 withholding to employee W-2s by January 31 following the tax year. Employers with 25 or more employees in the city must use the Collector’s electronic W-2 media specifications.
MO-ST-LOUIS.filing: Submit the quarterly returns to the Collector by mail, fax or email. File W-3 with W-2 detail. Send electronic W-2 media (CD or flash drive in the prescribed record format) to the Earnings Tax Division, City Hall Room 410, 1200 Market Street, St. Louis, MO 63103.
MO-ST-LOUIS.payment: Pay online and send the quarterly returns separately, or mail the returns with a check, cashier’s check or money order to the Payroll Expense Tax Department, PO Box 66966, St. Louis, MO 63166-6966.

DE-WILMINGTON.collector: City of Wilmington Department of Finance, Earned Income Tax Division
DE-WILMINGTON.registration: Request an employer account using the City's Earned Income Taxpayer Account Application.
returns: Quarterly withholding return
Report each calendar quarter by April 15, July 15, October 15 or January 15. Credit intermediate payments against the quarterly balance.
Intermediate withholding return
If withholding exceeds $50 in the first or second month of a quarter, report and remit that month's withholding by the 15th of the following month.
Annual reconciliation and W-2s
The city lists January 31 for paper W-2s and the end of February for electronic W-2s following the tax year. Confirm weekend deadlines with the Division.
DE-WILMINGTON.filing: Obtain periodic returns from the Division and submit them to City Finance. Employers with 50 or more city-taxable employees must file W-2 detail electronically. Use the secure upload linked in the City's W-2 instructions and include the RS record in the EFW2 file.
DE-WILMINGTON.payment: Pay the city by phone at (302) 576-2415 or (302) 576-2418, or in person at 800 N. French Street, 8th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801.

CO-DENVER.collector: City and County of Denver, Department of Finance, Treasury Division
CO-DENVER.registration: Register for Denver Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT) through Denver eBiz.
returns: Occupational Privilege Tax return

Report employee OPT withheld and business OPT owed by the employer. Rule 004 counts taxable employees, owners and partners. File monthly if the count reaches 10 in a month. Quarterly filing is available if the count stays below 10 each month. File and pay by the last day of the following month after each reporting period. Weekend and holiday deadlines move to the next business day.
Annual OPT return

Owner- or partner-only businesses with no employees liable during the year may file annually. Rule 004 gives January 31 following the tax year. The city FAQ also describes an advance-payment option. Check the period assigned to your account before paying.
CO-DENVER.filing: File the Denver OPT return through Denver eBiz for the period assigned by Treasury.
CO-DENVER.payment: Remit the employee and business portions through Denver eBiz with the return.

CO-GLENDALE.registration: Register the business in Glendale MUNIRevs.
returns: Occupational Privilege Tax return

File and pay by the 20th of the month after the assigned reporting period, including zero returns. The code specifies monthly filing above $60 per month and quarterly below $100 per quarter. Confirm the assigned period where neither condition applies. Annual filing requires Tax Inspector approval.
CO-GLENDALE.filing: Submit the city OPT return through Glendale MUNIRevs.
CO-GLENDALE.payment: Pay the employee and employer portions through Glendale MUNIRevs.

CO-GREENWOOD-VILLAGE.collector: City of Greenwood Village Taxpayer Services
CO-GREENWOOD-VILLAGE.registration: Apply online for an OPT license. Businesses using a PEO must obtain their own license and disclose the PEO.
returns: Occupational Privilege Tax return

File monthly by the last day of the next month. The Finance Director may permit less frequent employee withholding returns for employers whose monthly employee tax due is below $40. Confirm the schedule assigned to the account.
CO-GREENWOOD-VILLAGE.filing: Report both portions online through the Village tax payment portal, Xpress Bill Pay.
CO-GREENWOOD-VILLAGE.payment: Remit both portions through Xpress Bill Pay.

CO-SHERIDAN.registration: Register through Sheridan Business Licenses and confirm the OPT account with Finance at 303-762-2200.
returns: Occupational Privilege Tax return
File monthly by the last day of the following month, including zero returns. Employers with fewer than 10 employees may file quarterly. Confirm the quarterly due date on the city account.
CO-SHERIDAN.filing: Use Sheridan MuniRevs for the city's OPT return.
CO-SHERIDAN.payment: Remit employee withholding and the employer match to Sheridan via MuniRevs.

KY-LMRC.registration: Use EMINTS to register for a Louisville/Jefferson County tax account.
returns: Report quarterly withholding by the last day of the following month, including when monthly deposits are required.
W-1D
If withholding exceeds $3,000 in any quarter, deposit each month for the next four quarters. Deposits are due on the 15th of the following month.
Reconcile 2026 withholding and submit W-2 detail. February 28 falls on Sunday in 2027, so the next business day, March 1, is timely.
KY-LMRC.filing: File through EMINTS. Electronic W-1, W-2 and W-3 filing is mandatory for taxpayers filing more than 25 returns, forms or reports per year and preparers filing or expecting to file at least 10 per year.
KY-LMRC.payment: Pay LMRC through EMINTS and apply each deposit to its withholding period.

KY-LFUCG.collector: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, Division of Revenue
KY-LFUCG.registration: Apply for an occupational license before starting business using Form 228 IP.
returns: File quarterly by the end of the following month. If quarterly withholding exceeds $300, monthly returns are required. Use the monthly deadline on the assigned return.

Reconcile annually. KRS 67.783 sets February 28 as the statutory deadline. Use Revenue’s form for the 2026 tax year. Under KRS 446.030(2), the Sunday deadline for the 2026 reconciliation moves to Monday, March 1, 2027.
KY-LFUCG.filing: File payroll withholding online using the tax ID and LFUCG business number. Paper filers use the original periodic forms mailed to registered businesses.
KY-LFUCG.payment: Pay online by card or send ACH from your bank. Request banking instructions from Revenue and allow time for receipt by the due date.

KY-FCPS.collector: Fayette County Public Schools Tax Collection Office
KY-FCPS.registration: Use the district's questionnaire and initial reporting form to obtain the FCPS account number.
returns: Report withholding quarterly for Fayette County residents working in Fayette County. Use the district's 2026 quarterly form for each period.
File the annual school reconciliation and employee W-2 detail. Confirm the 2026 form and deadline with the school Tax Collection Office.
KY-FCPS.filing: Send the return to the school Tax Collection Office, PO Box 55570, Lexington, KY 40555-5570. After an online card payment, the district also accepts the return by fax at 859-422-9888.
KY-FCPS.payment: Pay payroll withholding through the district's card payment service using the FCPS account number. Send the return separately so the office can credit the payment.

KY-KENTON.collector: Kenton County Fiscal Court, Business Services
KY-KENTON.registration: Apply to Kenton County Business Services for an occupational license account. Confirm the worksite jurisdictions before preparing the county and participating city lines.
returns: QCC1

File by the last day of the month after each quarter. Report the county and each applicable city listed on the return. Include the employee detail required by the county. File the Covington city portion separately with Covington Finance.
KC-AR

Reconcile annually by February 28, even if payroll ceased during the year. Send W-2 copies with the reconciliation separately from the fourth-quarter return. Under KRS 446.030(2), the Sunday deadline for the 2026 reconciliation moves to Monday, March 1, 2027.
KY-KENTON.filing: Use the 2026 QCC1. Mail a quarterly return without payment to Kenton County Fiscal Court, PO Box 792, Covington, KY 41012. Use the mailing instructions on KC-AR for the annual reconciliation.
KY-KENTON.payment: For a quarterly return with payment, remit to Kenton County Fiscal Court, PO Box 706237, Cincinnati, OH 45270.

KY-COVINGTON.registration: Obtain a city occupational license and reporting number. Businesses physically located in Covington must first obtain zoning approval.
returns: Employer’s Return of License Fee Withheld

File monthly by the 15th of the next month if withholding exceeded $450 in any of the preceding four quarters. Otherwise file quarterly. Section 110.06(D) specifies the 30th of January, April, July and October. The quarterly form lists the last day of those months. Confirm with Finance before relying on a 31st deadline. Sign and return the form even for periods with no wages.
Employers’ Annual Reconciliation of License Fee Withheld

File by February 28 with federal W-2s and W-3 or an equivalent detailed employee listing. PEOs must supply a separate annual report for each client. Under KRS 446.030(2), the Sunday deadline for the 2026 reconciliation moves to Monday, March 1, 2027.
KY-COVINGTON.filing: Submit the signed city return to Covington Finance using the instructions on the city form. Employers operating in Covington also file with Kenton County.
KY-COVINGTON.payment: Remit the city withholding to the City of Covington with its return. The annual form directs remittances to 20 West Pike Street, Covington, KY 41011.

KY-BOWLING-GREEN.collector: City of Bowling Green, Office of Occupational License
KY-BOWLING-GREEN.registration: Submit a city business registration before starting work inside Bowling Green.
returns: City Employee Withholding Tax

File quarterly by the last day of the following month. If a quarterly payment exceeds $2,500, the city may assign monthly filing. Use the conversion date in the city notice. Monthly returns are due by the 15th of the next month.
Annual Reconciliation

File by February 28 with W-2s, W-3 and annual payroll register totals including deferred compensation. Under KRS 446.030(2), the Sunday deadline for the 2026 reconciliation moves to Monday, March 1, 2027.
KY-BOWLING-GREEN.filing: Use the city account number. Mail periodic returns to the Cincinnati lockbox. Send the annual reconciliation to the address on the annual form. Separately report wages and withholding for employees in designated special taxing districts.
KY-BOWLING-GREEN.payment: Include the payment with the return and make checks payable to City of Bowling Green. The periodic withholding lockbox is PO Box 643791, Cincinnati, OH 45264-3791.

KY-WARREN.registration: Apply for the county account using the Treasurer’s Occupational Business License Application.
returns: Quarterly Occupational Tax Return
File by the end of the month after each quarter. Sign and return the form even when no wages were paid. Weekend and legal holiday deadlines move to the next business day.
Annual Reconciliation Occupational Tax Return

Reconcile all four quarters and pay any balance. The February 28 deadline for 2026 wages falls on Sunday, so the county return is due March 1, 2027. Include W-2 and W-3 copies or equivalent employee detail accepted by the Treasurer.
KY-WARREN.filing: File the county forms with the Treasurer. The Treasurer’s website provides a link to send completed forms and a separate link for payments.
KY-WARREN.payment: Use Occupational Tax Online Payments or mail the signed return and payment to the Treasurer at the address printed on the county form.

KY-WARREN-SCHOOLS.collector: Warren County Public Schools Occupational Tax Office
KY-WARREN-SCHOOLS.registration: Submit the district’s Occupational License Tax Application. Use its residency certification or call the school tax office to verify the employee’s home school district.
returns: Quarterly Occupational Tax Return

School withholding applies to residents of the Warren County School District on wages earned in Warren County, including Bowling Green. File a signed quarterly return even for zero wages. The form lists January 31 for the fourth quarter.
Employers’ Annual Reconciliation of License Fee/Tax Withheld
File by February 28 with W-2s and W-3 or equivalent detail for all employees. Confirm weekend dates for 2026 filings with the district.
KY-WARREN-SCHOOLS.filing: Mail the signed school return to Warren County Public Schools, PO Box 51530, Bowling Green, KY 42102-5830. City and county returns are separate.
KY-WARREN-SCHOOLS.payment: Enclose school withholding with the signed return. Contact the school office for card or ACH instructions.

KY-OWENSBORO-DAVIESS.collector: City of Owensboro Occupational Tax Administrator, also administering Daviess County Fiscal Court withholding
KY-OWENSBORO-DAVIESS.registration: Obtain an occupational license before starting business. Use the business license application linked by Daviess County and contact Owensboro Finance for the withholding account and filing frequency.
returns: On the standard return, report wages earned inside Owensboro in column A and wages earned elsewhere in Daviess County in column B. Quarterly returns are due at the end of the next month. Monthly returns are due on the 15th of the next month except December, which is due January 31. For county withholding of $300 or more per quarter, switch to monthly filing upon notice from Finance.
REC

File by February 28 following the tax year. Complete separate reconciliations for city and county wages when both apply. Attach W-2s and W-3 or an equivalent employee listing showing wages and withholding by jurisdiction. The county moves weekend and legal holiday deadlines to the next business day. Under KRS 446.030(2), the Sunday deadline for the 2026 reconciliation moves to Monday, March 1, 2027.
KY-OWENSBORO-DAVIESS.filing: Submit the signed E-1 with the combined amount due to the Occupational Tax Administrator. For a worksite assigned to a tax increment financing district, obtain the applicable district form from Finance.
KY-OWENSBORO-DAVIESS.payment: Make the E-1 check payable to Occupational Tax Administrator and mail it with the return to PO Box 10008, Owensboro, KY 42302-9008.

AL-BIRMINGHAM.collector: City of Birmingham Finance Department, Tax and License Division
AL-BIRMINGHAM.registration: Register with the city for a taxpayer identification number. Use the Business License Application/Change Form to add an occupational tax account.
returns: Occupational Tax Return

File monthly by the 20th of the next month, including zero returns. If monthly withholding averaged less than $50 during the preceding calendar year, the employer may elect quarterly filing with the division. The due date is then the 20th following the quarter.
Annual Occupational Tax Reconciliation

City code section 3A-2-5(c) specifies January 31. Report each employee’s gross compensation, occupational tax withheld and remitted, and last known address. Confirm the annual filing date with the division for Sunday, January 31, 2027.
AL-BIRMINGHAM.filing: File periodic returns through Birmingham’s HdL Taxes Portal. The portal provides the annual reconciliation form.
AL-BIRMINGHAM.payment: Remit periodic withholding with the return through the city’s HdL Taxes Portal. The portal moves periodic weekend and holiday deadlines to the next business day.

AL-GADSDEN.registration: Submit the city business license application to Revenue and request the occupational withholding account.
returns: Occupational License Fee Return
Report and remit monthly withholding by the 20th of the following month.

Reconcile withholding and remittances for the calendar year by January 31. Include employee withholding statements, a listing or W-2s and explain any discrepancy. Confirm the annual filing date with Revenue for Sunday, January 31, 2027.
AL-GADSDEN.filing: File periodic occupational license fee returns through the TekConnectGov link on the city Revenue page. Mail the original annual G-3 and employee detail to City of Gadsden Revenue Department, PO Box 267, Gadsden, AL 35902.
AL-GADSDEN.payment: Pay periodic withholding through Gadsden’s TekConnectGov portal. Enclose any additional amount due with the G-3 reconciliation.

AL-AUBURN.registration: Use the city Tax Registration Form to establish the account and confirm its assigned filing frequency with Revenue.
returns: Employer’s Quarterly Return of Occupation License Fee

File for each assigned period, including zero wages. Quarterly returns are due on the first day of the month after quarter-end. The form allows filing through the last day of that month before delinquency.
Reconciliation of Occupational License Fee Withheld

The annual form lists January 1 as the due date and January 31 as the delinquent date. Attach Form W-3. If the employer paid the fee on employees’ behalf without withholding, include the employee detail requested on the form.
AL-AUBURN.filing: Submit the signed quarterly return with the city account number. Use the separate annual reconciliation to explain any difference in reported fees.
AL-AUBURN.payment: Make the quarterly check payable to City of Auburn and send it with the return to 144 Tichenor Avenue, Suite 6, Auburn, AL 36830.

AL-OPELIKA.registration: Apply for the city occupational license account using Opelika’s business license application.
returns: File quarterly even for zero wages. The city must receive the return and payment by the last day of the month after quarter-end. A postmark does not establish timely receipt.

File the original annual reconciliation by January 31 with employee statements, an equivalent listing or W-2 copies. Explain discrepancies in an attachment. The older 0-3 still prints 1.5%. The current quarterly form specifies 1% effective April 1, 2025. Use actual 2026 withholding when reconciling.
AL-OPELIKA.filing: Submit the quarterly return and separate annual reconciliation to City of Opelika Revenue Department, PO Box 390, Opelika, AL 36803. Confirm holiday or weekend receipt arrangements with Revenue before mailing.
AL-OPELIKA.payment: Make the quarterly check payable to City of Opelika and include it with the return.

AL-BESSEMER.registration: Use the city business license application and obtain the Bessemer taxpayer ID required on both returns.
returns: Occupational Tax Form

File quarterly and pay by the 20th of the month after quarter-end. File a zero return with an explanation when no wages were paid. Attach an explanation for wages excluded for services outside Bessemer.
Annual Occupational Tax Reconciliation Form
File the original by January 31 of the following year. List employee pay and withholding and the four quarterly remittances. Attach a statement explaining any difference.
AL-BESSEMER.filing: Submit the city forms to Bessemer Revenue Department, 1700 3rd Avenue North, Bessemer, AL 35020. Confirm weekend filing arrangements for the 2026 annual reconciliation.
AL-BESSEMER.payment: Send the quarterly return with a check or money order payable to City of Bessemer.

AL-LEEDS.collector: City of Leeds through Avenu Insights & Analytics
AL-LEEDS.registration: Contact Leeds Revenue or Avenu to establish the employer’s occupational withholding account. Use the assigned Avenu account number on the return.
returns: Occupational Tax Return
Report monthly withholding by the 20th of the next month. Use jurisdiction code 9401 for Leeds on the Avenu return.
Occupational Withholding Tax Annual Reconciliation Report
File by January 31 of the following year with W-2s, W-3 and the annual withholding summary. Attach an explanation of any difference between withholding and payments.
AL-LEEDS.filing: File periodic returns through the Avenu Taxpayer Portal or mail them to Avenu Tax Remittance Department. Use the separate Avenu annual form linked by Leeds. Confirm weekend filing arrangements for the 2026 reconciliation.
AL-LEEDS.payment: Remit monthly withholding through Avenu or with the mailed return. For a balance on the annual report, make the check payable to Tax Trust Account and send it with the signed form to PO Box 830725, Birmingham, AL 35283-0725.

OR-DOR-TRANSIT.registration: Before issuing paychecks, register for an Oregon business identification number (BIN) through Revenue Online or Combined Employer’s Registration. An existing employer entering a transit district reports the effective date on the Business Change in Status form.
returns: Form OQ

Report employer-paid district tax on the Oregon combined quarterly return. Allocate taxable wages by where services were performed, including remote work. Enter each district’s wages under its own designation (TM for TriMet, LTD for Lane). The statewide transit withholding tax has a separate entry.
2026 quarterly deadlines
File and pay by April 30 and July 31, 2026 for Q1 and Q2, November 2, 2026 for Q3, and February 1, 2027 for Q4.
OR-DOR-TRANSIT.filing: File the combined report through Frances Online or use paper Form OQ. Check the district boundary for each work location and the 2026 instructions for exemptions before reporting wages.
OR-DOR-TRANSIT.payment: Remit the employer tax to Oregon Department of Revenue by electronic funds transfer or use payment voucher OR-OTC-V with the combined payroll payment. Identify the district amounts and the payroll quarter.

OR-EUGENE.collector: City of Eugene, Community Safety Payroll Tax
OR-EUGENE.registration: Verify the employer’s physical business location using Eugene’s city limits address lookup. An employee working remotely from a Eugene home does not by itself establish a filing obligation for an employer with no business location in the city. Register through Eugene MUNIRevs and use the account number on paper returns.
returns: EUG-PY-1

File the employer payroll tax return quarterly. Include subject wages even when an employee is exempt from employee withholding. Eligible small employers may claim the reduced rate using EUG-RTR with the fourth-quarter or final return.
EUG-PY-2
File the employee withholding return quarterly, including when all employees are exempt. Submit EUG-ED employee detail with this return.
OR-EUGENE.filing: Submit both quarterly returns to Eugene through MUNIRevs or use the city’s 2026 paper forms. The filing and payment deadlines are April 30, July 31 and November 2, 2026, and February 1, 2027, under the city’s next-business-day rule.
OR-EUGENE.payment: Use online check or card in Eugene MUNIRevs. For paper filings, send the city voucher and a separate check or money order for each tax form to the address on that form.

OH-COLUMBUS.collector: City of Columbus Income Tax Division
OH-COLUMBUS.registration: Open an employer withholding account through CRISP at https://crisp.columbus.gov when you hire employees subject to city withholding.
returns: IT-11
File quarterly, including temporary periods without payroll while the account is active. The 2026 quarterly deadlines are April 30, July 31, November 2 and February 1, 2027.
IT-13
File the annual reconciliation with W-2 information by March 1, 2027. Include employees subject to Columbus withholding and those with courtesy withholding.
OH-COLUMBUS.filing: File through CRISP or use the city paper forms. For IT-13, upload W-2 images or a city-format fixed-width text file through CRISP, or submit paper wage detail per the instructions.
OH-COLUMBUS.payment: Federal next-day depositors remit electronically on the federal schedule. Otherwise remit semimonthly within three banking days after midmonth and month-end if prior-year withholding exceeded $11,999 total or $1,000 in any month. Otherwise remit monthly within 15 days after month-end if withholding exceeded $2,399 last year or $200 in any month of the prior quarter. Monthly depositors may remit the third month with IT-11. Remaining employers pay quarterly with IT-11. Pay via CRISP or, where permitted, by check with IT-11 or WH-PV. Send any balance separately from IT-13.

OH-CINCINNATI.collector: City of Cincinnati Income Tax Division
OH-CINCINNATI.registration: Verify the Cincinnati location against the city street guide. Open a Payroll Withholding account at https://web2.civicacmi.com/Cincinnati or send the New Account Application to the Income Tax Division using the email or fax printed on the form.
returns: Employer withholding coupons

Use the 2026 coupons for the applicable frequency. Remit semimonthly if prior-year withholding exceeded $11,999 in total or $1,000 in any month of that year. Payment is due on the third banking day after the 15th and after month-end. Otherwise remit monthly by the 15th of the next month if prior-year withholding exceeded $2,399 or any month of the preceding quarter exceeded $200. Other employers remit quarterly by the last day of the following month. See the electronic payment rule below.

Reconcile annual withholding and submit W-2 information. For 2026 wages the statutory February deadline falls on Sunday, so the reconciliation is due Monday, March 1, 2027 under Ohio Revised Code sections 718.03(H) and 1.14.
OH-CINCINNATI.filing: Use Cincinnati E-File for the reconciliation and W-2 submission. Employers required to submit federal W-2s electronically must submit Cincinnati wage information electronically. Use the city’s EFW2 instructions for file uploads.
OH-CINCINNATI.payment: City ordinance section 311-23(b)(iv) requires employers subject to federal electronic withholding deposits to remit accrued city withholding electronically when the federal deposit is due, unless granted a hardship exemption. Pay by ACH debit through Cincinnati E-File or enroll with the city for ACH credit. Where paper payment is permitted, mail a check payable to City of Cincinnati with the city coupon.

OH-TOLEDO.collector: City of Toledo Division of Taxation
OH-TOLEDO.registration: Complete the New Business Registration Form on the city income tax page to establish employer withholding.
returns: M-1 through M-12 / Q-1 through Q-4

Use monthly coupons when Toledo withholding or required withholding exceeded $2,399 last calendar year or $200 in any month of the previous quarter. Monthly deposits are due by the 15th of the next month. Otherwise use quarterly coupons, due by the end of the following month. The 2026 Q-4 coupon specifies February 1, 2027. The commissioner may assign semimonthly payments when last year exceeded $11,999 in total or $1,000 in any month. If assigned, remit by the third banking day after the 15th and after month-end.
Submit the annual reconciliation with W-2 information by March 1, 2027. Identify other municipalities and their withholding amounts on each W-2 or an attachment.
OH-TOLEDO.filing: File the periodic coupon for the assigned period. Upload annual wage data in EFW2 text format through the city website. Where paper filing is permitted, mail W-3 and the supporting W-2s to the Division of Taxation at the address printed on W-3.
OH-TOLEDO.payment: Federal electronic depositors must follow the city electronic filing and payment requirements. Use Ohio Business Gateway or ACH credit. A required electronic payment counts when credited to the designated account. For permitted paper deposits, use the coupon address for payments and make the check or money order payable to Commissioner of Taxation.

OH-DAYTON.registration: Mail or fax the New Business Questionnaire. Select Employee Withholding and Dayton City Limits and supply the FEIN. For eBill enrollment, request the existing city withholding account number from the tax office.
returns: DW-1

Monthly returns and payments are due on the 15th of the following month. Quarterly returns and payments are due by the last day of the following month. Dayton lists monthly filing above $2,399 last year or $600 last quarter. Ohio law also requires monthly remittance if withholding or required withholding exceeded $200 in any month of the preceding quarter, even if the quarter totaled $600 or less. Confirm the account schedule with Dayton if these tests differ.
DW-3
Reconcile 2026 withholding by March 1, 2027 under the Ohio Sunday rule. Include W-2s or an equivalent listing and applicable 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC copies. Pay any balance separately.
OH-DAYTON.filing: Use the city DW-1 for Dayton wages. Submit zero returns through the city zero-withholding portal. Mail DW-3 to the address on the form. The DW-3 requires electronic media for 100 or more employee records. Confirm the 2026 electronic media specifications with Dayton because its forms page currently lists 2025 specifications.
OH-DAYTON.payment: Use eBill, bank-initiated ACH or Ohio Business Gateway. The city payment portal excludes paper checks and credit cards.

OH-CANTON.collector: City of Canton Income Tax Department
OH-CANTON.registration: Complete the Business & Corporation Information Sheet. Select City of Canton and provide the FEIN, employee count, payroll and any third-party filer information.
returns: Return of Income Tax Withheld

Quarterly payments are due at the end of the following month. Canton's 2026 booklet specifies monthly payments by the 15th of the following month at $200 or more in any month or above $2,399 the prior year. It specifies semimonthly payments at $1,000 or more in any month or above $11,999 the prior year. For each half-month, pay by the third banking day after it ends. Ohio Revised Code 718.03 uses strictly above $200 in any month of the preceding quarter and above $1,000 in any month of the preceding year. Confirm the assigned frequency with Canton if the tests differ.

File the annual reconciliation with employee W-2 information by March 1, 2027 under Ohio's Sunday rule. Canton's forms directory currently lists the 2025 W-3. Obtain the 2026 version or instructions from the department.
OH-CANTON.filing: Use the city's annual reconciliation upload portal for electronic wage reporting. For permitted paper periodic returns, sign and mail the dated coupon to the Income Tax Department. Indicate periods with no employees and submit supporting documentation.
OH-CANTON.payment: Federal electronic depositors must remit electronically. Canton accepts ACH debit, ACH credit using specifications from the department, and Ohio Business Gateway. Make permitted paper payments payable to City of Canton.

OH-AKRON.collector: City of Akron Income Tax Division
OH-AKRON.registration: Return the city business registration questionnaire with your FEIN, start date, payroll provider and Akron employee count. Sole proprietors also complete the individual questionnaire.
returns: EFT withholding

Remit quarterly by the last day of the month after quarter-end unless monthly filing applies. For 2026 Q4 the next business day is February 1, 2027. Remit monthly by the 15th of the following month if prior-year withholding exceeded $2,399 or withholding exceeded $200 in any month of the preceding quarter.
AW-3

File the annual reconciliation with employee W-2 records. The ordinary 2026 deadline is March 1, 2027 because February 28 falls on Sunday. The city form allows until March 31 when the employer properly supplies all required W-2 fields on CD in an accepted data format. Confirm the current media instructions with the division before using the extension.
OH-AKRON.filing: File periodic withholding electronically. For the annual reconciliation follow AW-3 instructions for paper W-2s or structured wage data. The city rejects electronic W-2s submitted as PDFs or images.
OH-AKRON.payment: Enroll for city EFT through the Akron withholding portal. Record each transaction confirmation and select the city account for city wages. Joint economic development districts have separate accounts.

OH-AKRON-JEDD.collector: City of Akron Income Tax Division for the selected JEDD
OH-AKRON-JEDD.registration: Select the district on the JEDD Business Registration questionnaire and return it within ten days of receipt. Include your FEIN, district worksite, start date and payroll provider. Obtain a separate withholding account for each district.
returns: JEDD EFT withholding

Pay quarterly by the last day of the following month. The Q4 2026 deadline is February 1, 2027. Pay monthly by the 15th of the following month if withholding for the district exceeded $2,399 in the prior calendar year or $200 in any month of the preceding quarter. The EFT worksheet moves weekend and holiday due dates to the next business day.
JW-3
File a separate annual reconciliation for each district with its employee W-2 information. The ordinary 2026 deadline is March 1, 2027 under the Ohio Sunday rule.
OH-AKRON-JEDD.filing: File periodic withholding electronically using the district account. On JW-3 select the matching district and report its deposits. Submit paper W-2s or wage data in an accepted format. Akron rejects PDF and image copies of W-2s.
OH-AKRON-JEDD.payment: Enroll for debit EFT through the Akron withholding portal. Select the account for the district where the wages were earned and keep the confirmation number.

OH-DAYTON-MIAMI-JEDD.collector: City of Dayton Finance Department for the Miami Township-Dayton JEDD
OH-DAYTON-MIAMI-JEDD.registration: Send the New Business Questionnaire by mail or fax. Select Employee Withholding and provide the FEIN and worksite address. The district names do not appear among the location boxes. Confirm the correct selection with Dayton at 937-333-3500.
returns: DW-1 MT-DAY JEDD

Monthly returns and payments are due on the 15th of the following month. Quarterly returns and payments are due by the last day of the following month. Dayton lists monthly filing above $2,399 last year or $600 last quarter. Ohio law also requires monthly remittance if withholding or required withholding exceeded $200 in any month of the preceding quarter, even if the quarter totaled $600 or less. Confirm the account schedule with Dayton if these tests differ.
DW-3

Reconcile 2026 withholding by March 1, 2027. The district coupon refers employers to DW-3 for W-2 reporting. The published DW-3 shows Dayton city payroll and its city rate. Ask Dayton how to report district wages and deposits before completing those lines.
OH-DAYTON-MIAMI-JEDD.filing: Sign the MT-DAY JEDD coupon for the period and report only payroll and withholding for the Miami Township-Dayton district. Keep Dayton city withholding separate.
OH-DAYTON-MIAMI-JEDD.payment: Mail the district coupon with a check or money order payable to City of Dayton to PO Box 643700, Cincinnati, OH 45264-3700. Pay previously reported balances separately.

OH-DAYTON-BUTLER-JEDD.collector: City of Dayton Finance Department for the Butler Township-Dayton JEDD
OH-DAYTON-BUTLER-JEDD.registration: Send the New Business Questionnaire by mail or fax. Select Employee Withholding and provide the FEIN and worksite address. The district names do not appear among the location boxes. Confirm the correct selection with Dayton at 937-333-3500.
returns: DW-1 BT-DAY JEDD

Monthly returns and payments are due on the 15th of the following month. Quarterly returns and payments are due by the last day of the following month. Dayton lists monthly filing above $2,399 last year or $600 last quarter. Ohio law also requires monthly remittance if withholding or required withholding exceeded $200 in any month of the preceding quarter, even if the quarter totaled $600 or less. Confirm the account schedule with Dayton if these tests differ.
DW-3

Reconcile 2026 withholding by March 1, 2027. The district coupon refers employers to DW-3 for W-2 reporting. The published DW-3 shows Dayton city payroll and its city rate. Ask Dayton how to report district wages and deposits before completing those lines.
OH-DAYTON-BUTLER-JEDD.filing: Sign the BT-DAY JEDD coupon for the period and report only payroll and withholding for the Butler Township-Dayton district. Keep Dayton city withholding separate.
OH-DAYTON-BUTLER-JEDD.payment: Mail the district coupon with a check or money order payable to City of Dayton to PO Box 643700, Cincinnati, OH 45264-3700. Pay previously reported balances separately.

OH-JEFFERSON-WASHINGTON-CH-JEDD.collector: City of Washington Court House Tax Department for the Jefferson Township-Washington Court House JEDD
OH-JEFFERSON-WASHINGTON-CH-JEDD.registration: Complete the 2026 JEDD Business Questionnaire and submit it to the city Tax Department at 117 N Main St, Washington Court House, OH 43160. Confirm the account and filing frequency at 740-636-2342.
returns: Use the district coupon for the assigned period. Quarterly payments are due at the end of the month following the quarter. Monthly payments are due by the 15th of the following month when prior-year withholding exceeded $2,399 or any month of the prior quarter exceeded $200, counting amounts required to be withheld. For semimonthly accounts, check the district coupon against the statutory third banking day after each half-month. Confirm any earlier printed date with the department.

Reconcile 2026 withholding by March 1, 2027 under the Ohio Sunday rule. The department lists a 2025 district W3 requiring W-2s. Request the 2026 district form and W-2 submission instructions before filing.
OH-JEFFERSON-WASHINGTON-CH-JEDD.filing: Sign and mail the district W1 to the Tax Department at 117 N Main St, Washington Court House, OH 43160. The city describes Ohio Business Gateway filing for net profits. Confirm electronic withholding arrangements directly with the department.
OH-JEFFERSON-WASHINGTON-CH-JEDD.payment: Enclose a check or money order payable to Jefferson Township-Washington Court House JEDD with the district coupon.
